title: Signed or unsigned?
description:
Choose the right jumps:

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `max_signed(a, b)` | the larger as signed numbers: `max_signed(-1, 1)` is 1 |
| `max_unsigned(a, b)` | the larger as unsigned numbers: `max_unsigned(-1, 1)` is −1 (the largest unsigned value) |
| `is_digit(c)` | 1 if c is `'0'` to `'9'`, else 0, using **one** unsigned comparison |
| `in_range(x, low, high)` | 1 if low <= x <= high (signed, low <= high), else 0, with one subtraction and **one** unsigned comparison |
| `valid_index(i, length)` | 1 if 0 <= i < length (both signed numbers), else 0, with **one** comparison |

starter.solution.asm:
max_signed:
        mov     rax, rdi
        ret

max_unsigned:
        mov     rax, rdi
        ret

is_digit:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

in_range:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

valid_index:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
max_signed:
        mov     rax, rdi
        cmp     rdi, rsi
        jge     .done
        mov     rax, rsi
.done:  ret

max_unsigned:
        mov     rax, rdi
        cmp     rdi, rsi
        jae     .done
        mov     rax, rsi
.done:  ret

is_digit:
        xor     eax, eax
        sub     rdi, '0'
        cmp     rdi, 9
        ja      .done
        mov     eax, 1
.done:  ret

in_range:
        xor     eax, eax
        sub     rdi, rsi                ; x - low
        sub     rdx, rsi                ; high - low
        cmp     rdi, rdx
        ja      .done                   ; below low wraps to a huge number
        mov     eax, 1
.done:  ret

valid_index:
        xor     eax, eax
        cmp     rdi, rsi
        jae     .done                   ; a negative i looks huge
        mov     eax, 1
.done:  ret

hints: Signed comparisons use `jg`/`jl` (or `cmovg`), unsigned ones `ja`/`jb` (or `cmova`). That is the whole difference between the two `max` functions.
The one-comparison range trick: subtract the lower bound, then compare unsigned with the size of the range. A value below the bound wraps round to a huge unsigned number, so it fails the same test.
rules: Use the unsigned jumps where they fit.
unitTests:
test "signed maximum"
    max_signed(-1, 1) == 1
    max_signed(5, 3) == 5
    max_signed(-10, -20) == -10
test "unsigned maximum"
    max_unsigned(-1, 1) == -1
    max_unsigned(5, 3) == 5
    max_unsigned(0, 0x8000000000000000) == 0x8000000000000000
test "digits"
    is_digit('0') == 1
    is_digit('9') == 1
    is_digit('5') == 1
    is_digit('/') == 0
    is_digit(':') == 0
    is_digit('a') == 0
    is_digit(0) == 0
test "a range in one compare"
    in_range(5, 1, 10) == 1
    in_range(1, 1, 10) == 1
    in_range(10, 1, 10) == 1
    in_range(0, 1, 10) == 0
    in_range(11, 1, 10) == 0
    in_range(-5, -10, -1) == 1
    in_range(-11, -10, -1) == 0
    in_range(-1000, 1, 10) == 0
test "valid indexes"
    valid_index(0, 5) == 1
    valid_index(4, 5) == 1
    valid_index(5, 5) == 0
    valid_index(-1, 5) == 0
    valid_index(0, 0) == 0

rules.message: Use the unsigned jumps where they fit.
